_comment: GLM-5.3 Flash prefill roofline-vs-measured. Per-op 'measured' = that decoder-layer block's GEMM-FLOPs / its measured wall-time (effective GEMM throughput of the block), from the roofline FLOP budget (glm5_flash_prefill_roofline.json: kda 433.9, moe 579.8, mla 128.8, dense 231.9 GFLOP) and the shipping TIMEIT leaves (382001, GNR gnrap, 8-layer proxy, M=256). roofline_target = measured GNR AMX bf16 dense-GEMM peak 14927.2 GFLOP/s. HONEST CAVEAT appended to the .md: this dense-GEMM FLOP ceiling is the hardware max but is NOT the right target for the recurrence-dominated KDA (dispatch/small-op bound; even a native AMX kernel ~ torch compute) -> the realistic engineering floor is ~4s (fused CPU KDA kernel), not 0.09s. The low per-op efficiency localizes WHERE FLOP-throughput is lost (small-M KDA/MoE/MLA) vs the one near-efficient block (big-M dense MLP).
precision: fp8 e4m3 block W8A16, bf16 compute
constants_source: plugin/validate/glm5_prefill_roofline.py (measured GNR AMX bf16 GEMM peak = 14927 GFLOP/s)

ops.note: per-chunk per-head matmuls; dispatch-bound. FLOP-roofline NOT the right ceiling — realistic floor ~4s via a fused CPU KDA kernel.
~M*topk/E tokens/expert (small M); batching / operating-point lever (cf. DSv4 MoE).
big contiguous dense-MLP GEMMs — the one near-efficient block (~10x the small-M ops).
